evidence.restatement: Pollock's drip paintings were made by pouring and flinging paint onto unstretched canvas laid on the floor.
Rothko painted colour fields, Warhol made silkscreens and Hopper painted realist scenes; none made floor drip paintings.
Pollock worked in a converted barn beside his house at Springs, East Hampton, on Long Island.
He used commercial and household enamel paints, applied with sticks, hardened brushes and syringes as he moved around the canvas.
Pollock became famous for pouring and dripping paint onto canvas laid flat on the floor.
Rothko painted colour fields, Hopper realist scenes and Warhol pop art; none worked by dripping onto a floor canvas.
